Each cohort is compared against itself in the previous term, when the stricter standard applied, so the relaxed marking and the tutoring blocks moved together. items.confound_note: Every case measures coursework submission rates, not exam pass rates. Handing in coursework is not passing an exam: tutoring blocks can raise the share of students who submit their coursework by 4 to 8 points while the share who pass the exam stays flat or falls, since submission is a matter of turning work in and passing is a matter of graded performance. The claim is about exam pass rates, so none of the four cases bears on it.
items.notes: Closing sentence is verbatim identical to both TRUE items; the conditions are identical to diverse_true. The ONLY change is the measured-quantity phrase, 'exam pass rates' becoming 'coursework submission rates' in all four cases. Check that the substitute is genuinely non-equivalent to the claimed quantity and that its wording is unique to this family.
